The research notebook records an experiment about grouped-query attention. Several query heads share each key-value group, so their retention choices must be accounted for together. One observation is a probability distribution over the input positions. A low-entropy head is concentrated, while a high-entropy head distributes attention across many positions. Concentration alone does not prove factual relevance. The experiment compares page selections under a fixed group quota, records each configuration, and preserves the full observations so another researcher can reproduce the computation. Which assumptions need to hold before selected-page counts can be interpreted as physical memory savings?
